newsitem.title: USA: US spot MTBE firm on tight supplies, firm gasoline.
newsitem.headline: US spot MTBE firm on tight supplies, firm gasoline.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices firmed this week on the back of tight supplies and strong gasoline values, industry sources said.

They noted that the rise in U.S. Gulf September MTBE, to about 84.50 cents a gallon this week, was as much a result of short supply and fundamental factors as it was the run-up on gasoline, which was prompted by military action in Iraq.
The reported shutdown of a 12,500 bpd MTBE plant in Texas for the next two weeks along with talk that two major plants will go into planned maintenance this month has kept buyers in the market.
Traders note that the coming start of the October-to-January oxygenated fuels season and will keep demand high, especially since few import barrels are seen coming from the U.K.
"The potential is for more demand in the very near future, and prices are going to continue to rise," explained one trader who noted that feedstock prices are also firm.
But another trader was more wary noting that prices may stagnate until demand picks up, and could fall if already volatile gasoline prices fall from their current lofty levels.
In New York Harbor, prompt MTBE was pegged at 87.50 cents.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
